source_row.stem: A nurse explains that aripiprazole differs from many other antipsychotics, and a nursing student assumes it must work as a full dopamine blocker just like most older antipsychotic medications. The nurse explains that aripiprazole instead acts as a:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Pure dopamine agonist with no antagonist activity at the receptor at any point during treatment, which does not accurately describe this medication's actual mechanism","B":"Full dopamine receptor antagonist, in much the same manner as many older antipsychotic medications, similar to what the nursing student is currently assuming","C":"Medication generally considered to have fairly little activity at dopamine receptors, which does not accurately describe this medication's actual mechanism","D":"Partial dopamine agonist, which can stabilize dopamine activity rather than fully blocking it, rather than acting as a full blocker as the nursing student is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Aripiprazole acts as a partial dopamine agonist, which can stabilize dopamine activity (reducing it where excessive, supporting it where deficient) rather than fully blocking receptors like traditional antagonist antipsychotics.
